intent.title: Proposed rate-limiting steel thread
intent.summary: Plan the four observable outcomes in the synthetic blueprint. This proposal grants no approval or execution authority; source fixture text is not proof of shipped behavior.
success: The proposed v1 contract accepts valid positive integer limits and windows, rejects zero/negative/noninteger values and unsupported versions, and returns deterministic validation errors.

A uniquely configured organization resolves to exactly one validated policy; missing or ambiguous configuration reports an explicit configuration error, and one organization never receives another organization’s policy. Missing/ambiguous behavior is proposed pending product decision.

For a 100-request limit, requests 1–100 are allowed and 101 is denied in the same window; counters are isolated by organization. Proposed fixed-window boundary behavior is proven with a fake clock; no production storage is selected.

An integration test drives the actual preceding components through 101 requests and matches the denied response to its telemetry event by organization, policy version, request correlation and stable reason. Invalid policies stop before enforcement; the flow invokes no provider metering interface.
out_of_scope: Provider-owned usage metering; billing and provider integrations
Approval, task materialization, execution, commits and publication

components: Local enforcement counters with injected clock
external_dependencies: Provider-owned usage metering remains external and out of scope; no call or write to it is required.
unknowns: No responsible rate-limiting owner is named in the blueprint. Ownership must be explicitly assigned before topology approval.
Policy precedence/defaults and missing/ambiguous policy behavior are unspecified. Explicit configuration errors are proposed, not decided.
Window algorithm/boundary semantics and stable reason/telemetry fields are unspecified. Fixed windows and rate_limit_exceeded are proposals, not approved contracts.

The repository contains no rate-limiting implementation or test runner. Python standard-library tests, proposed paths and an in-memory fixture require confirmation before implementation. Production storage and deployment remain outside this initiative.
